tasks.title: A closure module (IIFE)
tasks.statement: Create a variable counter that holds the result of an immediately invoked function: an object with the methods inc() (increments the counter and returns it), reset() and value(). The counter itself must not be reachable from outside. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: var counter = (function () { var n = 0; return { … }; })();

tasks.title: Polyfill for Function.prototype.bind
tasks.statement: Write a function bindFn(fn, ctx) (extra arguments are remembered): it returns a function that calls fn with this = ctx, first with the remembered arguments and then with the ones passed later. You must not use the bind method. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments, 2) and fn.apply(ctx, …)

tasks.title: Polyfill for Object.create (Crockford's way)
tasks.statement: Write a function objectFrom(proto): it returns a new empty object whose prototype is proto. You must not use Object.create: use a temporary constructor. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: function F() {} F.prototype = proto; return new F();

tasks.title: map, ES3 style
tasks.statement: Write a function mapES3(arr, fn, thisArg): it returns a new array of the results of fn.call(thisArg, element, index, array) for each element; holes in a sparse array are skipped (and stay holes in the result). You must not use the map method. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Check i in arr — that is how holes are skipped.

tasks.title: filter, ES3 style
tasks.statement: Write a function filterES3(arr, pred, thisArg): it returns a new array of the elements for which pred.call(thisArg, element, index, array) is truthy; holes are skipped. You must not use the filter method. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: i in arr && pred.call(thisArg, arr[i], i, arr)

tasks.title: reduce, ES3 style
tasks.statement: Write a function reduceES3(arr, fn, init): it folds the array from left to right; if init is not passed (arguments.length < 3), the first element serves as the initial value; for an empty array without init, throw a TypeError. You must not use the reduce method. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: arguments.length tells “init not passed” apart from “init is undefined”.

tasks.title: Polyfill for indexOf
tasks.statement: Write a function indexOfES3(arr, x, from): the index of the first element strictly equal to x, starting at position from (0 by default); a negative from counts from the end; if nothing is found, -1. You must not use the indexOf method. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Normalize from: if it is negative, use max(0, n + from).

tasks.title: Polyfill for trim
tasks.statement: Write a function trimES3(s): it removes whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, newlines) at the start and end of the string using a regular expression. You must not use the trim method. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: s.replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, "")

tasks.title: Polyfill for Object.keys
tasks.statement: Write a function keysES3(obj): an array of the object's own enumerable keys in for…in order; skip inherited keys (hasOwnProperty). You must not use Object.keys. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Check Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, k) inside for (var k in obj).

tasks.title: Your own call via a temporary property
tasks.statement: Write a function callFn(fn, ctx) (the remaining arguments are passed to fn): it calls fn so that this inside is ctx, without call, apply or bind. Tip: put fn into a temporary property of ctx and call it as a method, then delete it. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: ctx[key] = fn; ctx[key](…); delete ctx[key]. Passing an arbitrary number of arguments was solved in ES3 with eval — or handle the needed number of cases by hand.

tasks.title: Query string: parsing and building
tasks.statement: Write the functions parseQuery(s) (“a=1&b=%D0%B0&c”, a leading “?” is allowed) → an object with string values (a missing “=” gives an empty string; a repeated key keeps the last value) and buildQuery(obj) → a string “k=v&k2=v2” encoded with encodeURIComponent. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: split("&"), then split("="); do not forget decodeURIComponent and encodeURIComponent.

tasks.title: Parsing document.cookie
tasks.statement: Write a function parseCookies(str): a string like “a=1; b=hello%20world; c=” → an object; spaces around pairs are dropped, values are decoded with decodeURIComponent, pairs without “=” are skipped. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: split(";"), then indexOf("=") — the value may contain “=”.

tasks.title: Mini-jQuery over a node list
tasks.statement: Page nodes are modeled as objects { tag, classes: [...], text }. Write a function $(nodes, selector): it returns a wrapper object with the members length (a number — no getter needed, just a field), each(fn(node, i)), addClass(c), removeClass(c), text() (the texts of the found nodes joined with a space) and text(value) (write). All mutating methods return the wrapper (chaining). Selectors: “tag”, “.class”, “tag.class”, “*”. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Split the selector on “.”, filter the nodes and return an object whose methods return itself.

tasks.title: A model of XMLHttpRequest
tasks.statement: Write a constructor FakeXHR(server): server is an object “address → {status, body}”. Methods: open(method, url) (readyState = 1), send() (synchronously goes through states 2, 3, 4; after each it changes readyState and calls onreadystatechange if it is set; at 4 it fills in status and responseText; an unknown address gives status 404 and an empty responseText). The initial readyState = 0. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: A single method _set(state) describes “change the state + callback”.

tasks.title: Error-first callbacks
tasks.statement: Write a function getJson(http, url, cb): http.get(url, function (err, text)) is a request (asynchronous); getJson calls cb(err) if the request fails, cb(null, object) if the JSON parses successfully, and cb(err) with a SyntaxError for invalid JSON. cb must be called exactly once, even if cb itself throws an exception. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Catch the exception from JSON.parse separately so that cb is not called twice (a try around cb itself is a mistake).

tasks.title: series: tasks one by one
tasks.statement: Write a function series(tasks, done): tasks are functions of the form function (cb) { … cb(err, result) }; run them strictly one after another (the next one after the previous one calls its cb); done(err, results) is called once: after the last task with an array of results, or right at the first error with that error. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: A recursive function next() that takes the next task and passes it a callback that calls next().

tasks.title: parallel: tasks at the same time
tasks.statement: Write a function parallel(tasks, done): it starts all the tasks (function (cb) { … cb(err, result) }) at once; done(err, results) is called once: when all have finished — with results in task order (not completion order), or at the first error. An empty array calls done(null, []) immediately. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: A counter of remaining tasks and a closure with the index; a finished flag protects against a second done.

tasks.title: Detecting the browser by User-Agent
tasks.statement: Write a function detectBrowser(ua): it returns “ie” (contains “MSIE” or “Trident/”), “edge” (“Edg/” or “Edge/”), “opera” (“OPR/” or “Opera”), “chrome” (“Chrome/” — a Chrome string also contains “Safari/”), “firefox” (“Firefox/”), “safari” (“Safari/” without “Chrome/”) or “unknown”. The order of checks matters. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Chrome, Edge and Opera contain both “Chrome/” and “Safari/” — check them before the plain ones.

tasks.title: Script inclusion order
tasks.statement: Scripts depend on each other: [{ name: "app.js", needs: ["plugin.js", "jquery.js"] }, …]. Write a function scriptOrder(scripts): it returns an array of names in an order where every script comes after its dependencies (when choosing among ready ones, keep the original list order); on a dependency cycle it throws Error("cycle"), and on a dependency on an unknown script, Error("no script: <name>"). Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Depth-first traversal with three node states: not visited, in progress, done.

tasks.title: Namespaces (YUI style)
tasks.statement: Write a function namespace(root, path): path is a string like “app.ui.menu”; it creates nested empty objects in root along the parts of the path (existing ones are not overwritten) and returns the deepest one. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Walk the path parts, creating an object wherever the field does not exist yet.

tasks.title: Inheritance via a prototype (ES3)
tasks.statement: Write a function inherit(Child, Parent): it sets up the prototype chain so that instances of Child inherit the methods of Parent.prototype, without calling Parent and keeping Child.prototype.constructor === Child. If Child.prototype already has methods, they need not be preserved — it is called before the methods are declared. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: A temporary constructor F with F.prototype = Parent.prototype; Child.prototype = new F().

tasks.title: extend, jQuery style
tasks.statement: Write a function extend(target, …sources) and a deep-merge variant: if the first argument is true — extend(true, target, a, b) — it recursively merges nested plain objects (arrays and everything else are replaced whole). It returns target. undefined values are skipped. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: arguments[0] may be a boolean flag; in deep mode call extend recursively for nested objects.

tasks.title: PubSub, jQuery-plugin style
tasks.statement: Write a function createPubSub(): it returns an object with the methods subscribe(topic, fn) → token (a number, growing from 1), publish(topic, data) → the number of subscribers called (subscribers are called in subscription order, fn(data, topic)) and unsubscribe(token) → true/false (whether such a token existed). Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: The token is a unique id; unsubscribe looks it up across all topics.

tasks.title: ECMAScript editions
tasks.statement: Write a function ecmaInfo(name): it accepts “ES3”, “ES5”, “ES6”, “ES2015”, “ES2020”, … and returns an object { edition, year }. Rules: ES1 — 1997, ES2 — 1998, ES3 — 1999, ES5 — 2009 (ES4 was cancelled — for it throw Error("ES4 not released")); starting with ES6, edition n came out in 2009 + n (ES6 = ES2015, ES7 = ES2016, …); “ES<year>” (year ≥ 2015) gives edition = year - 2009. Invalid names — Error("unknown edition"). Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: The regular expression /^ES(\d+)$/ and a table of early editions {1: 1997, 2: 1998, 3: 1999, 5: 2009}.

tasks.title: XML versus JSON
tasks.statement: Write a function toXml(name, obj): a flat object turns into XML: toXml("user", {id: 1, name: "Ada"}) → «<user><id>1</id><name>Ada</name></user>». Escape the characters &, <, > in values as & < >. And a function compareSize(obj) → { json, xml } — the lengths of the two representations (JSON.stringify and toXml("o", obj)). Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Order of replacements: & first (otherwise you will escape your own ampersands), then < and >.

tasks.title: debounce for the resize event
tasks.statement: Write a function debounce(fn, ms): it returns a function that postpones the call of fn by ms milliseconds after the last invocation (each new invocation resets the timer); fn is called with the arguments and this of the last invocation. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: clearTimeout(timer) before a new setTimeout; save this and arguments into local variables.

tasks.title: typeOf, Crockford style
tasks.statement: Write a function typeOf(v): it returns “null”, “array”, “date”, “regexp”, “function”, “error”, “object” (for other objects) or the result of typeof for primitives; use Object.prototype.toString. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Object.prototype.toString.call(v).slice(8, -1)

tasks.title: Memoization, ES3 style
tasks.statement: Write a function memoizeES3(fn): it returns a function that caches the result by a key — the arguments joined with JSON.stringify(Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments)). A repeated call with the same arguments does not call fn. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: hasOwnProperty is more reliable than checking the value: the result may be 0 or undefined.

tasks.title: compose and pipe, ES3 style
tasks.statement: Write a function composeES3(f, g, h, …): it returns a function that applies the given functions from right to left (like mathematical composition); with no arguments it is the identity function. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Loop over the saved array of functions from the end.

tasks.title: Currying, ES3 style
tasks.statement: Write a function curryN(fn, n): it returns a function that can be called in parts (curryN(f, 3)(1)(2)(3), curryN(f, 3)(1, 2)(3), and so on); once n arguments have been collected, it calls fn with them and returns the result. Write in ES3 style: only var and function — no arrow functions, let/const, classes, template strings or spread.
tasks.hint: Accumulate arguments in an array until there are n of them.
